note.question: How do inventory constraints affect bundling in a dynamic pricing setting, challenging the classical view that bundling consistently enhances revenue?
note.overview: This paper studies the impact of inventory constraints on bundling in a dynamic pricing setting, challenging the classical view that bundling consistently enhances revenue. Traditional bundling theory, which typically assumes abundant inventory and static pricing, often asserts that bundling generates higher revenue than selling products individually. However, we show that limited inventory, in fact, distorts the revenue-extraction capability of bundling, favoring the sale of products or services separately.
